title: Image Type
description: Image objects with acquisition details and component type classification. Typed as ada:image and schema:ImageObject.

ada:componentType.description: ADA componentType for an image, as a single string. Allowed values are constrained at the technique-profile level.

schema:width.description: Width of the raster, in pixels.

schema:height.description: Height of the raster, in pixels.

ada:illuminationType.description: Type of illumination used to create the image. Examples include Visible light, Cross-polarized visible light, ultraviolet light, Electron beam, X-ray.

ada:imageType.description: Specifies the nature of the sample's response to the illumination that was detected and measured.

ada:spatialRegistration.description:
Pixel size and its units. SCALING ONLY -- the half of a spatial registration an unregistered image can state. A plain image has a pixel size, and ada:pixelScaleX on an ada:EPMAImage is a well-formed statement, but an image does not say where it sits on the sample or how its axes relate to the sample axes. The imageMap block references the full shape, which adds the origin, the origin corner, the coordinate definition and the two rotation terms, and whose required list demands them.
Same property NAME on both branches on purpose: a placement path such as schema:hasPart[@type=ada:image|ada:imageMap].ada:spatialRegistration.ada:pixelScaleX then resolves through either, which is what the subject-key register and the TAPP sidecars both target. Before this, the image branch declared no spatialRegistration at all -- not because a pixel scale is meaningless on an image, but because the only available shape required an origin and a corner, so an image could not use it without asserting a registration it does not have.

PixelDimension.title: Pixel Dimension
PixelDimension.description:
A raster dimension in pixels, as a schema:QuantitativeValue. ONE declaration, referenced by every block that needs it, so the shape cannot drift between them -- which it already had: geochemProduct declared schema:width as this object while a draft technique block declared it as anyOf[integer, string], and a value satisfying either violated the other. Nothing caught that, because the two blocks are validated separately.
A QuantitativeValue rather than a bare integer, following the reason geochemProduct already records: the same schema.org property carries physical dimensions elsewhere, so the unit has to be stated rather than assumed to be pixels -- and schema:size beside it already takes this shape.
schema:width and schema:height are used in preference to the ada: equivalents they replace (ada:numPixelsX, ada:numPixelsY), because a schema.org property that applies is preferred to a minted one.
ada:pixelSize was listed here as a third replaced property, and that was wrong twice over. It is not a pixel COUNT, so schema:width and schema:height cannot express it -- the paragraph above is exactly why, since a property whose unit must be STATED rather than assumed cannot also be the property that states the count. What supersedes ada:pixelSize is the other axis entirely: ada:spatialRegistration.ada:pixelScaleX / ada:pixelScaleY with ada:pixelUnits, the SCALING half this block already references from spatialRegistration/$defs/Scaling, whose title is "Pixel Scaling" and whose description is "pixel size and its units". That form is the better one -- it separates the two axes, so an anisotropic pixel is sayable, and it carries the unit in a property of its own, which "0.5 micrometer" as one string does not. This block's example has been migrated accordingly, to pixelScaleX/Y of 0.5 with ada:pixelUnits "micrometer", and image/rules.shacl now asks for the scaling rather than for ada:pixelSize.
The claim that came with it, "nothing is lost: no example carried the ada: forms", was false for every one of the three, and the examples have now been migrated so that it is true. Measured over examples.yaml and example*.json before the move: ada:pixelSize in image/examples.yaml, ada:numPixelsX/Y in imageMap/examples.yaml AND supDocImage/examples.yaml, against schema:width in only the three STEM detail examples. The counts were declared here in their schema.org form while two examples still wrote the ada: form, and they validated solely because neither block is sealed -- so nothing reported it. All three now carry the schema.org forms, and the three shapes ask for them: imageMap and supDocImage for schema:width / schema:height, this block for ada:spatialRegistration.
